summary: This note is a Wikipedia-based overview of the New York Yankees, an American professional baseball club based in the Bronx that plays in the American League East. It covers the franchise's origins as the 1901 Baltimore Orioles, its move to New York as the Highlanders, and its 1913 renaming. It also describes the 2009 season, including the opening of the new Yankee Stadium, several free-agent signings, and the team's 27th World Series title.
one_line: Overview of the New York Yankees, the Bronx-based MLB American League East club, covering its founding history and 2009 championship season.
key_facts: The New York Yankees are an American professional baseball team based in the New York City borough of the Bronx.
The Yankees compete in Major League Baseball as a member club of the American League East division.
The Yankees are one of two major league clubs based in New York City; the other is the New York Mets of the National League.
In the 1901 season, the club began play in the American League as the Baltimore Orioles, a team with no relation to the modern Baltimore Orioles.
Frank Farrell and Bill Devery purchased the franchise, which had ceased operations, and moved it to New York City, renaming it the New York Highlanders.
The Highlanders were officially renamed the Yankees in 1913.
During the off-season, the Yankees signed star free agents including CC Sabathia, Mark Teixeira, and A.J. Burnett.
At the beginning of the 2009 season, the Yankees opened the new Yankee Stadium, located just a block north on River Avenue from their former home.
The Yankees set a major league record by playing error-free ball for 18 consecutive games from May 14 to June 1, 2009.
The Yankees finished first in the AL East.
In the ALDS, the Yankees defeated the Twins in a sweep.
In the ALCS, the Yankees defeated the Angels in six games.
The Yankees defeated the defending champion Philadelphia Phillies in Game 6 of the World Series by a score of 7-3, taking the series 4-2.
The 2009 World Series win was the Yankees' 27th World Series title.
